utterances.text: And can you tell us where that is? I mean it's not possible to see it, I don't think, on the ELMO, but --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: It's on the far right, far right side of the machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the counter, can you tell us where that is on the machine?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: It's -- it's also ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, great. We can see it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: The counter is here, the speed control is here, and then these are the just play controls for recording and stopping, pausing, rewinding, forwarding.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. There's also what appears to be a level meter, right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is there volume control?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And appears to be also a tone control?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you just cry for the Court if you can recall, and as brief a manner as you can, how it is that tape is actually threaded and played?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE
utterances.text: Yes. There is an empty reel-to-reel on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we need to go through this. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have all used something like that, given our age.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have. I have. Just one question. Did it have the possibility of deleting, wiping out tape --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could go back and record over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With that I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. McCloskey is not agreeing with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, everyone, but Ms. Stewart alerted to me through a slight problem we've gotten ourselves into. As you know it is a practice for a witness not to speak to the Prosecutor mid-testimony. We really need to speak to Ms. Frease about her upcoming testimony, about the exhibits, so we can get prepared, and I should have thought of that beforehand so we could request the Court to waive that particular practice. I don't see any prejudice to anyone if that practice is waived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any submissions from the Defence teams? All right. So permission is granted. Of course you have to use your good judgement and, I mean, you know what the rules of the game are, and you are not to abuse of any of them. So there is nothing else Ms. Frease wanted to show us. I think it's just one machine she had with her or more than one machine?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just one machine that she had with her. Well there is the other machine that's actually -- that actually played the recordings, but I don't know that it's necessary for the Court to examine that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The understanding was that there will not be any cross-examination today. Those are pleasures yet to come when Ms. Frease returns. But if there is anything that would you like to ask today, maybe in relation either to the two tapes or to the machine that we have just been shown or anything else, you are free to do so. I see that there is no such desire or intention, which basically means, Ms. Frease, that you are free to go. You will of course return in due course to proceed with your testimony. I wish to thank you for having come over and I wish you a safe journey back to wherever you are going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there anything else, any further business you would like to transact?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one brief statement. If I could invite the Defence attorneys, we are bringing in, I believe it's February, several archaeologists, anthropologists and pathologists. I would invite the Defence if they have any stipulations that they may find me easier to stipulate than getting your point out of these witnesses, and they will be very repetitive because they all did the same thing, the diggers and the pathologists, and if there is any point, they're coming in from all over the world and we planned for that, and -- but if anyone -- any last-minute effort to make some stipulations on some of this material and some of the issues that have come over and over again, we appreciate it, we work with that, because that is going to be a fair amount of time, court time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that's a good suggestion. I suppose that I -- I just recommend to the Defence teams to try and think about this and hold discussions with Mr. McCloskey with a view to streamlining the procedure as much as possible. All right. We will reconvene Monday. I think we are sitting in the morning. We are sitting in the morning. So Monday. Thank you, and have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
